summary: Gives rules for downgrading X.400 1988 messages to the older 1984 form when they carry MIME content types. It replaces chapter 6 of RFC 1328 and leaves the rest of that document in place. It is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1496 explains how gateways can carry MIME content when mail moves between X.400(88) and X.400(84). They convert content when possible and wrap unsupported parts in a text form that preserves the encoded content.

subtitle: Rules for carrying MIME content through an older X.400 mail system.

tldr.problem: X.400(84) cannot directly represent every body part that can appear in X.400(88) or MIME mail.
tldr.mechanism: A gateway converts what it can and encapsulates unsupported body parts in an IA5 text body part with MIME headers and encoded content.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates the downgrading rules in chapter 6 of RFC 1328, and the unit metadata marks this document Historic.

today: The unit metadata marks RFC 1496 as Historic. It records rules for downgrading MIME-bearing mail between X.400 versions and updates chapter 6 of RFC 1328.

sections.title: Handling Content an Older System Cannot Represent
sections.content:
X.400(88) and MIME can contain body parts that X.400(84) cannot adequately represent. RFC 1328 already described downgrading between the two X.400 versions, but did not specify what to do with these unsupported parts.

RFC 1496 modifies the earlier rules for mail moving between SMTP with MIME and X.400(84). It replaces chapter 6 of RFC 1328; the rest of that RFC is not obsoleted by this document.
sections.plainLanguage: Older X.400 systems may not understand every kind of MIME content. This RFC adds rules for carrying that content through the conversion.

sections.title: Convert or Encapsulate the Body Part
sections.content:
The gateway should convert content when the older format can represent it, encapsulate content when conversion is not possible, and avoid dropping a message. Body parts that are already defined in X.400(84) should remain in their existing form.

For an unsupported body part, the gateway creates an IA5Text body part with MIME-Version, Content-Type, and Content-Transfer-Encoding headers, followed by the encoded content. On the reverse path, an IA5 body part beginning with MIME-Version is converted according to the referenced MIME mapping rules.
sections.plainLanguage: The gateway keeps content in its original form when it can. If the older system cannot use a part directly, the gateway wraps it with MIME information and encoded data.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says security concerns described in the referenced MIME and X.400 mapping documents also apply to these conversions. In particular, a mail user agent that automatically starts programs in response to content can expose a user to trojan programs.

The document does not define a new mechanism for authenticating or protecting the encapsulated body part.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail software should be careful about automatically running programs based on message content. The conversion rules do not remove that risk.
